questions.title: If the Detroit Tigers trade Tarik Skubal by the 2026 MLB trade deadline, which team will acquire him?
questions.background: Tarik Skubal is a starting pitcher for the Detroit Tigers and is eligible for free agency after the 2026 season.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official MLB or team announcements, or confirmed reporting from ESPN, identifying a completed trade of Tarik Skubal by the 2026 MLB trade deadline. Resolution : Resolve to the MLB club acquiring Skubal directly from the Detroit Tigers. If no such trade occurs by the deadline, the question is void. Tampa Bay Rays trim slightly 0.17 -> 0.15: still Big Three with Shane McClanahan exiting Thursday's start with mid-back tightness adding urgency, tempered by reluctance to move Top-10 OF Theo Gillen and 10% Kalshi odds. Atlanta Braves ease 0.11 -> 0.08 (Passan/Feinsand second tier behind Big Three, 6% Kalshi). Chicago Cubs enter #5 at 0.07 replacing Philadelphia Phillies (0.06): MLB.com lists Dodgers/Brewers/Rays/Cubs as primary suitors, Passan names Skubal Chicago's best fit, The Athletic's Patrick Mooney reports Cubs considering him as their blockbuster option, and Feinsand explicitly downgraded Phillies and Yankees to 'long shots.' Leaves 14% residual for Phillies, Yankees, Orioles, Mets, Red Sox, Padres, and mystery teams.

local_articles.title: Peter Malnati takes early lead in 8th and final Rocket Classic in Detroit
local_articles.snippet: Tour this season, filling his head with doubts about his game. He just got quite a confidence boost. Malnati shot a career-best, 9-under 61 to tie a tournament record in the first round of the final Rocket Classic on Thursday, giving him a two-shot lead. When Malnati stood on the first tee, his caddie suggested leaving the driver in his bag to play it safe and set up a solid start. Malnati, though, went against the advice and used his driver to put a tee shot in the middle of the fairway that set up his first of seven birdies on the front nine. "Even in the beginning, before I knew it was going to be a special day, I didn't feel the same level of like anxiety," he said. With thoughts of a sub-60 round crossing his mind, he made a 55-foot putt for birdie at No. 11 and was nine under through 13 holes before missing some putts down the stretch in a bogey-free round. questions.title: Which month of 2026 will have the highest ICE arrest total in the data publicly available by August 26, 2026?
questions.background: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) carries out arrests as part of federal immigration enforcement.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Use government data supplied by ICE, as reported by The Associated Press. Resolution Date : Resolve to the calendar month of 2026 with the largest arrest total among the months covered by the latest ICE monthly figures publicly available by August 26, 2026. Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the month name only.
questions.current_reasoning: 2026-07-29 update with 29 of 31 days of July elapsed and no new ICE Detention Management release yet (next regular cycle expected Aug 3; full-month July requires an Aug 10-24 update): Local reporting from July 28-29 confirms late-July arrest operations accelerated rather than faded after July 1-11's 1,593/day pace (which only requires 1,281/day over July 12-31 to beat June's 43,138, well below June's 1,438/day pace). Specifically, CBS News (July 29) reported expanded TSA-ICE civil-immigration airport arrests explicitly described by ICE sources as a straightforward way to boost arrest totals under White House pressure to hit 2,000 daily arrests; Reuters/Straits Times (July 28) detailed thousands of arrests via reversed ORR child-sponsor data-sharing safeguards; and DHS Secretary Mullin boasted of single-day records while Haitian TPS ended mid-month. Conditional on full-month July data being publicly available by Aug 26 (~68% probability, accounting for irregular 2026 release gaps and OHSS executive director Marc Rosenblum's July 28 resignation), July's conditional probability of beating June improves from ~86% to ~91%, lifting July 0.59 -> 0.62 and trimming June 0.39 -> 0.36 while holding January (0.01) and August (0.01).

questions.title: Which international organization, if any, will first gain direct access to Aung San Suu Kyi in detention during 2026?
questions.background: Aung San Suu Kyi has been detained since Myanmar's military overthrew her government in February 2021. Her access to outside visitors has been tightly restricted.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Public statements from the visiting organization or Myanmar authorities, corroborated by established news reporting. Qualifying Event : Direct access means a completed in-person meeting with Suu Kyi by a representative acting on behalf of an international organization. Permission or an announced plan without a completed visit does not qualify. Resolution : Resolve to the first international organization publicly confirmed to have completed such a visit during 2026. If no qualifying visit is confirmed by December 31, 2026, resolve that no organization qualified. Accepted Answer Format : The organization's name, or a statement that no organization qualified.
questions.current_reasoning: 2026-07-29 update (first check since July 22; 57.5% of 2026 now elapsed with zero access breakthroughs across Exa and regional coverage): New July 23-29 reporting significantly strengthens 'No organization qualified' (0.61 -> 0.67): (1) Reuters/Straits Times/AsiaOne (July 23-24) reported ASEAN Special Envoy / Philippine FM Maria Theresa Lazaro saying Myanmar leaders' return to ASEAN meetings is 'still far off,' that Myanmar's pro-military Parliament formally passed a motion rejecting ASEAN's five-point consensus as 'interference,' and that while she will lead a humanitarian mission later in 2026, it is 'not certain' she will be granted access to Suu Kyi; (2) ACLED (Straits Times July 27) documented a sharp escalation in junta civilian massacres under new military chief Ye Win Oo as the regime consolidates control; and (3) Mandalay courts sentenced nine peaceful activists to 27-37 years on July 28-29 (Al Jazeera) over election protests demanding release of political prisoners after the coup against Suu Kyi. With ~3.6 years of total incommunicado detention and hardening regime posture, ASEAN trims 0.25 -> 0.22 (still clear #1 among organizations given Lazaro's planned later-2026 mission and Min Aung Hlaing's Aug 6-7 Bangkok visit), ICRC trims 0.08 -> 0.06, UN trims 0.03 -> 0.02, and WHO holds 0.01 (2% residual).

local_articles.title: Myanmar’s Min Aung Hlaing criticises ASEAN, sets out government agenda
local_articles.snippet: lined his government’s plans for the war-torn Southeast Asian country. Myanmar was plunged into turmoil in February 2021 when the military ousted an elected government led by Nobel Peace Prize winner Aung San Suu Kyi, sparking protests that expanded into a protracted civil war, killing some 100,000 people and displacing millions. At the turn of 2026, the military engineered a widely criticised election won by an army-backed party that allowed Min Aung Hlaing to transition into a civilian role. Dismissing ASEAN’s peace plan – known as the “Five Point Consensus” – Min Aung Hlaing said the 11-member grouping has discriminated against Myanmar. “We have been patient. We will respond to non-constructive actions on a case-by-case basis,” he said, without referring to any specific member of the Association of South-east Asian Nations.
